correctness.rationale: The cosine samples are strictly ordered on the half-grid, so the quadratic with roots at the adjacent samples \(3n\) and \(3n+1\) is nonnegative everywhere. Two positive weights at those nodes eliminate the second-harmonic coefficient and produce an exact dual upper certificate. The signs \(\cos(2r\theta)<0<\cos(2s\theta)\) give positivity of the weights, and elementary trigonometric identities yield the closed form. The inspected verifier checks these identities for \(1\le n\le100\), but the proof is analytic for all \(n\ge2\).
